summary.intent: Test whether switching from flatfs to pebbleds storage backend improves reliability under high concurrency (75 clients), after flatfs was failing with 10 errors and timeouts.
summary.outcome: The 75-client pebbleds test was fired off and was still running at session end. The session was complicated by discovering 3 duplicate API processes running concurrently, which were cleaned up down to one (PID 70577). A transient DB health check timeout occurred during cleanup but recovered.

repo: The API can accumulate zombie pnpm wrapper processes from multiple dev launches; only one can hold port 3000 but the others persist as orphaned processes.
pebbleds is being evaluated as a replacement for flatfs due to concurrency/reliability issues at scale.
At 75 clients, sequential SDK + flatfs produced 10 errors and timed out — the baseline for comparison.
workflow: Background task notifications (task-notification tags) surface failed background processes; cross-reference with current process list before acting on them.
After killing duplicate API processes, a transient DB health check timeout can occur but recovers quickly — wait and recheck before escalating.
Use port listeners + process list together to identify true duplicates vs. zombie wrappers.

friction: Three duplicate API server processes were running concurrently due to multiple dev launches, causing confusion about which was active.
Duplicate processes hung on SIGTERM and required SIGKILL.
Transient DB health check timeout occurred immediately after killing the duplicate processes, creating uncertainty about whether the ongoing test results would be valid.
open_items: 75-client concurrent SDK + pebbleds test results still pending at session end — need to confirm whether it outperforms the flatfs baseline (10 errors, timeout).
ROADMAP.md and STATE.md were modified — review to confirm they reflect current test plan and pebbleds evaluation status.
No guard against accidentally launching multiple API server instances during development; worth adding a check or using a process manager.
